templates.title: Which ingredient formulation is approved for the next artwork revision?
templates.question: The artwork declares Honey (1%) while the specification sheet states Honey (9%). Which recipe percentage is authoritative for production?
templates.reason: Honey percentage conflict between specification and artwork directly blocks QUID compliance and recipe substantiation.

templates.title: Can R&D confirm the calculation basis for the Nutrition Facts values?
templates.question: Nutrient declarations appear to mix per-serving (85g) and per-100g amounts. Can R&D confirm the authoritative analytical basis?
templates.reason: Mismatched nutritional measurement basis blocks valid % Daily Value calculations and Atwater energy plausibility screening.

templates.title: Does the approved formula support the 'No Added Sugar' marketing claim?
templates.question: The packaging displays a 'No Added Sugar' claim, but the ingredient list includes Honey, Coconut Sugar, and Crystallized Ginger (cane sugar). Does Legal approve this claim?
templates.reason: Under 21 CFR 101.60(c)(2), foods containing added sugars or sugar-containing ingredients cannot claim 'No Added Sugar'.

templates.title: Can Legal confirm the tree-nut ingredient and precautionary allergen wording?
templates.question: Almonds and pecans are intentional recipe ingredients, but also appear in the 'May Contain' advisory statement. Can Legal verify if this advisory wording should be corrected?
templates.reason: Listing intentional recipe ingredients in a 'May Contain' statement creates consumer confusion and contradicts FDA allergen labeling guidance.
answerOptions: Remove intentional nuts from advisory statement
Retain current wording per QA risk assessment

templates.title: Can Brand confirm whether the vegan claim is authorized and adequately substantiated?
templates.question: The artwork declares 'Suitable for Vegans' but also declares Honey as an ingredient. Does Brand authorize this dietary claim for the US market?
templates.reason: Honey is an animal-derived ingredient; unqualified vegan claims on honey-containing products face regulatory challenge and consumer objection.

templates.title: Can the product owner confirm the approved serving size and servings per container?
templates.question: The panel declares 8 servings at 85g per serving (totalling 680g), but the package net weight is 480g. Which value represents the verified product packaging?
templates.reason: Arithmetic inconsistency between serving size, serving count, and package net weight violates 21 CFR 101.9(b).
answerOptions: Adjust serving size to match net weight

templates.title: Can Legal confirm the applicable target market and launch date?
templates.question: The launch date determines regulatory transition windows and enforcement dates. Please confirm the scheduled commercial release date.
templates.reason: Regulatory rule pack applicability relies on the effective date interval.

templates.title: Which existing brand design elements must remain unchanged in the next revision?
templates.question: Review the detected design assets (logo, colors, tagline) and indicate whether each should be KEPT, CHANGED, ADDED, or REMOVED in the creative brief.
templates.reason: Directly feeds the future packaging design brief.
